whatContradictedTheCard: The card's framing implicitly treated 'panel effective dates absent from NFHL entirely' (R3's own words) as a source-level fact. It is true only of the one layer R3 queried; NFHL as a whole carries EFF_DATE on a sibling layer in the same service. Recharacterizing 'absent from NFHL' as 'absent from the layer we asked' is the load-bearing correction in this close.

The card's target list did not mention a preliminary/pending service existing at all (it asked to scout 'preliminary/pending panels for the six counties' as if that were a filter or attribute on the known service). It is a wholly separate top-level service (PrelimPending/), discovered only by fetching the REST catalog root rather than assuming the known service's structure was complete.

LESSON: Before treating a data gap as 'needs external acquisition,' fetch the SAME service's own layer catalog (?f=json at the MapServer root) -- ArcGIS REST services routinely expose dozens of sibling layers under one URL, and a prior loader querying one layer number is not evidence the others were considered and rejected.
returnCountOnly=true against a public ArcGIS REST endpoint is a cheap, fast way to size a target before committing to a build estimate -- use it before guessing magnitude from unrelated context.

A JS-only viewer (FEMA's Estimated BFE Viewer) is not itself a data source; look for the underlying state/agency GIS service that likely backs its map (TWDB's Texas_BLE_Status here) rather than treating 'the viewer is JS, so this can't be scouted' as a dead end.

Do not hand-estimate checkpoint/close timestamps. This card's own CP1/CP2 'at' fields were written as plausible guesses rather than queried live, and the close's original closedAt (16:35:00Z) turned out to be LATER than the actual real time (16:14:25Z) when it was checked minutes later for an unrelated reason -- a fabricated future timestamp in a durable artifact, caught only by accident. `date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ` is one Bash call; there is no excuse to guess.
